## Glue Constraints

### What it does
This graph demonstrates both basic voronoi fracturing and then using glue constraints to both cluster the resulting shards and to constrain the shards with a different strength based on position.

### Inputs and outputs
This graph is self-contained, the mesh is a mesh cube.  The output is a rigid body simulation.

### How it works
The base of the simulation (cube) is fractured using points that are denser in the center than the outside of the cube ("point_shaping").  The fractured shards are constrained with a glue constraint whose strength is driven by the distance to the impact point, as well as the *active_state* of the rigid bodies being masked by the same distance.  This is then simulated with a kinematic collider from below.
